land.text: Khwarazm, a Seljuk governorship: 'Seljuk rule in Khwarazm (r. 1042-1077)' (Seljuk dynasty page), whose governorship 'fell into the hands of Anush Tigin Gharchai' in 1077

predecessors.note: A Seljuk province until the shahs made themselves independent in practice; the Anushtegin page gives the governorship in 1077 and the first full reign (Qutb ad-Din Muhammad) from 1097.

land.text: the shahdom of Khwarazm under Ala ad-Din Muhammad (Muhammad II), with Khorasan and western Iran

successors.note: Cliopatria splits one line of shahs into this row (1094-1201) and a 'Khwarezmid Empire' row (1202-1235), different Wikidata ids (Q486918 and Q63134381); the two dossiers name each other as predecessor and successor and a reviewer may merge them.

capitals.name: Gurganj (Kunya-Urgench)
capitals.note: The pages name Gurganj as the capital only at the end: Muhammad II 'shifted his capital from Gurganj to Samarkand' in 1212 (Anushtegin page) and Tekish returned to Gurganj in 1200 and was buried there (Tekish page); Sanjar-Shah was exiled to Gurganj in 1187. The years before 1172 are my assumption (confidence 1).

rulers.note: The governorship 'fell into the hands of Anush Tigin Gharchai' in 1077; the end year is the next reign's start (1097) minus one, his death is not dated on the page.

rulers.name: Qutb ad-Din Muhammad I (Arslan Tigin Muhammad)
rulers.note: Regnal table '1097-1127/28'; Atsiz is dated 1127 (infobox) so the handover is shown at 1127.

rulers.name: Atsiz (Qizil Arslan Atsiz)
rulers.note: Infobox reign '1127 - 30 July 1156'; the Atsiz page text has him succeed in 1127 or 1128.

rulers.name: Tekish (Ala ad-Din Tekish)
rulers.note: 'officially became Khwarazmshah on 11 December 1172'; died 3 July 1200 of a peritonsillar abscess.

rulers.name: Ala ad-Din Muhammad (Muhammad II)
rulers.note: Named heir by Tekish as Qutb ad-Din Muhammad, who took the name Ala ad-Din Muhammad; his reign continues in the khwarezmid-empire dossier.

correction.text: Khwarazm, governed for the Seljuks by Anush Tigin Gharchai from 1077

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1077-1093: Cliopatria's row starts only in 1094 although the Anushtegin page's founding year is 1077 (governorship of Anush Tigin Gharchai) and its table gives the first full reign from 1097. Nothing on the pages gives the extent before 1094; the core is Khwarezm itself. Confidence 1 for the extent; it overlaps the Great Seljuk shape, which holds Khwarezm in those years.

correction.text: the 1094 shape without the lower Syr Darya, which Atsiz adds in 1138

keyframe_review.note: 614,269 km2 for 1094-1146: Khwarezm, the Karakum and Kyzylkum margins and the lower Syr Darya at Jand (Qyzylorda 56%). The Atsiz page puts the lower Syr Darya and Mangyshlak in 1138 (he also conquered them that year), so for 1094-1137 the Syr Darya part is taken out (the Qyzylorda oblast, where Jand lies). The Anushtegin page gives no area figure (it says only 'large parts of present-day Central Asia, Afghanistan and Iran' for the empire years).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1138-1146: after 'In 1138, he rebelled openly against his suzerain' Atsiz conquered Mangyshlak and the lower Syr Darya that year. Cliopatria's 1094 shape has the Syr Darya but not Mangyshlak (0%).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1147-1151: Cliopatria has no Khwarezmid shape for these years and draws Khwarezm as Great Seljuk land. The Atsiz page has Sanjar force Atsiz back into vassalage in 1143 and undertake 'another expedition against Atsiz in 1147 when the latter became rebellious again', with no result; the shape here is Khwarezm itself, a vassal under the Great Seljuk tint (great-seljuk-empire vassal events, 1143-1152). [fx-04, 2026-11-01] Mangyshlak and the lower Syr Darya added: Atsiz 'conquered the Mangyshlak and lower bank of the Syr Darya' in 1138 and the Atsiz page records no loss of either before the Qara Khitai band took Jand in 1152 (ledger 1152, 'recaptured Jand ... in April'); the keyframes 1138-1146 and 1152-1201 hold both, so this one did too, and without them the keyframe snap of 1147 released the land and the Kimek shape claimed it for 1147-1151.

correction.text: the 1152 shape with Mangyshlak and the lower Syr Darya (Jand)

keyframe_review.note: 492,767 km2 for 1152-1168: Khwarezm and the Turkmen plains, with Merv (90%) but without Mangyshlak or the Syr Darya. The Atsiz page has Atsiz hold Mangyshlak and the lower Syr Darya from 1138 and recapture Jand in April 1152 from a Qara Khitai band, so both are added. Merv in these years is unverified: the Tekish page has Soltan-Shah (a Khwarezmid prince) capture Merv by 1180 and Tekish take it only in December 1193.

Tekish 'endeavored to siege Nishapur again on 27 March 1187, and it fell two months later'; Sanjar-Shah, with his atabeg Mengi-Tegin, had held it from 1185 and was sent to exile in Gurganj. keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1193: 'Tekish captured Ray in January 1193'; the commander of Sarakhs 'surrendered the town to him' in 1193; Merv was captured in December 1193 after Soltan-Shah's death (19/29 September) and Tekish's son Malik-Shah was made its governor.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1194-1199: Tekish defeated and killed Tughril III at Rayy on 4 March 1194 and held Persian Iraq, including Isfahan, by 25 June 1194. The caliph's army took Hamadan, Ray and (late 1195) Isfahan and Tekish won Hamadan back on 15 July 1196, so 1195-1196 is a gap in the ledger, drawn here as the held shape; after 1196 Tekish gave Mayachuq 'governorship over all of Persian Iraq'.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1200-1201: after Tekish's death (3 July 1200) the Ghurids took control of all Khorasan (Seljuk Empire page, dated 1200). The Persian Iraq and Ray holdings stand; the Ghurid dossier has Muhammad II recover parts of Khorasan by 1201 (a Muhammad II page was not opened here).

ledger.note: 1077: Anush Tigin Gharchai becomes governor of Khwarazm. The governorship 'fell into the hands of Anush Tigin Gharchai' in 1077 (Anushtegin page; infobox founding year 1077), after 'Seljuk rule in Khwarazm (r. 1042-1077)' (Seljuk dynasty page). Cliopatria draws the row only from 1094; the table's first full reign, Qutb ad-Din Muhammad, begins 1097.

1138: Atsiz rebels and Sanjar marches on Khwarezm. 'In 1138, he rebelled openly against his suzerain' (Atsiz page); 'In 1138, Sanjar marched with his army to Khwarezm and defeated Atsiz and his army in the Battle of Hazorasp' (Sanjar page, 2nd page). Sanjar installed Suleiman Shah, who 'was unable to hold on to the province' when Atsiz returned.

union.text: the lower Syr Darya at Jand

region.text: Mangyshlak and the lower Syr Darya

ledger.note: 1138: Atsiz conquers Mangyshlak and the lower Syr Darya. The page says he also conquered Mangyshlak and the lower Syr Darya that year and annexed Mangyshlak and Jand to Khwarazm. The page names no former holder; the Kipchak-Kimek confederation is the nearest Cliopatria neighbour (1094-1146).

1141: Atsiz invades Khorasan after Qatwan. He took advantage of the defeat to invade Khorasan, occupying Merv, Nishapur and Sarakhs (Atsiz page: the defeat is Qatwan, 9 September 1141, Qatwan page); after Qatwan Khwarazm 'became a vassal state of the Kara-Khitan' (Qatwan page; the kara-khitans dossier opens the vassalage in 1142).

1142: Sanjar expels Atsiz from Khorasan. 'In 1142, Atsiz was expelled from Khorasan by Sanjar.' The Qara Khitai raided Khwarazm the same year and forced Atsiz to pay 30,000 dinars a year (Qatwan page).

1143: Sanjar subdues Khwarezm again. Sanjar invaded Khwarazm 'in the following year' [1143] and forced Atsiz back into vassalage (Atsiz page; Sanjar page: 'Sanjar then marched to Khwarezm with his army in 1143'). In 1147 Sanjar led 'another expedition against Atsiz ... when the latter became rebellious again'; neither page gives the result.

region.text: Jand on the lower Syr Darya

ledger.note: 1152: Qara Khitai occupy Jand. 'In 1152, Jand was occupied by a band of the Qara Khitai.'

region.text: Jand on the lower Syr Darya

ledger.note: 1152: Atsiz retakes Jand in April. Atsiz recaptured it in April (Atsiz page). He 'continued to pay tribute to the Kara Khitai until his death' in 1156.

1180: Sultan-Shah holds Merv against his brother Tekish. Soltan-Shah captured Merv by 1180 (Tekish page); Mahmud Sultan Shah, 'a younger half-brother and rival of Tekish in Upper Khurasan', is the rival of 1172-1193 (Anushtegin page); in May 1181 he conquered Tus. The year is the page's 'by 1180'.

1187: Tekish takes Nishapur. He 'endeavored to siege Nishapur again on 27 March 1187, and it fell two months later'; Sanjar-Shah, who had held it since 1185 with the atabeg Mengi-Tegin, went into exile at Gurganj and Mengi-Tegin was executed.

1193: Sarakhs surrenders. In 1193 the commander Bahr ad-Din Chaqir surrendered the town to Tekish (Tekish page), who had already stormed and destroyed its fortress when Sultan-Shah took refuge there (after 1190).

1193: Tekish takes Ray. 'Tekish captured Ray in January 1193, followed by the Tabrak citadel after 2 day siege', at the request of Qutlugh Inanch; Toghrul III then offered to become a vassal and hand over Ray.

1193: Tekish takes Merv after Sultan-Shah's death. Sultan-Shah 'died on 19/29 September 1193'; 'Tekish pounced on the opportunity and captured Merv in December, making his son Malik-Shah the governor.'
1193: the rivalry with Sultan-Shah ends with Merv in Tekish's hands (December 1193).

1194: Tekish defeats and kills Tughril III at the Battle of Rayy, 4 March. Tughril III attacked on 4 March 1194 and was defeated and killed; the Seljuk Empire infobox dates 'Battle of Ray and the supplantation by the Khwarazmian Empire' to 1194.
1194: the struggle for Ray ends with Tughril III's death.
1194: the Khwarazmians hold Persian Iraq, including Isfahan, by 25 June. Rayy, Hamadan and Isfahan pass from the last Great Seljuk sultan.

1195: the caliph's army retakes Persian Iraq. Ibn al-Qassab's army was beaten at the Asadabad Pass but Tekish 'returned to Khwarazm in 1195'; the caliphal forces took Hamadan and Ray and 'In late 1195, Isfahan and the rest of Persian Iraq fell to the Caliph'.

1196: Tekish wins Hamadan back. After Ibn al-Qassab died in July he won 'on July 15' and Hamadan surrendered on 18 July; 'the rest of the territory was given to Uzbek ibn Muhammad, Yunus-Khan and Mayachuq' and later all of Persian Iraq to Mayachuq. Gokcha kept his territories as an Eldiguzid subject.

1198: Tekish besieges Herat. The caliph had told the Ghurid Ghiyath al-Din Muhammad to invade; the Ghurids took Balkh in 1198 and Tekish 'embarked from Tus to besiege Herat', then 'made peace with the Ghurids and the Caliph'. The year is the page's 1198.
1198: Tekish makes peace with the Ghurids and the caliph.
1199: Tekish crushes Mayachuq's revolt in Mazandaran. In January 1199 Mayachuq and his supporters 'locked themselves in the fortress of Ardahn in Mazandaran'; Tekish stormed it and executed them.
1199: the revolt ends with Mayachuq's execution at Ardahn.

1200: the Ghurids take Khorasan after Tekish's death. the Ghurids took control of all Khorasan after Tekish died (Seljuk Empire page); Tekish died on 3 July 1200 and Muhammad II succeeded (Tekish page). Muhammad II won Khorasan back in 1204 after the Ghurid defeat at Andkhud (Seljuk Empire page), outside this dossier.

region.text: the shahdom of Khwarazm under Muhammad II

ledger.note: 1201: the shahs pass into the 'Khwarezmid Empire' row. Cliopatria ends the Khwarezmid Dynasty row in 1201 and starts the Khwarezmid Empire in 1202; the Anushtegin page treats one line of shahs, with the 'Khwarazmian Empire' of 1077-1231 in its infobox. The cut is Cliopatria's.

wars.name: Atsiz's rebellion against Sanjar
wars.outcome: Hazarasp (1138): Sanjar wins and installs Suleiman Shah, who cannot hold the province; Atsiz returns, submits in 1141, invades Khorasan after Qatwan, is expelled in 1142 and made a vassal again in 1143; Sanjar marches again in 1147.

wars.name: Battle of Qatwan and the Qara Khitai raid on Khwarezm
wars.outcome: Qara Khitai defeat Sanjar on 9 September 1141; Khwarazm becomes their vassal and pays 30,000 dinars a year after a raid in 1142.
wars.note: No border moves; the vassal relation is opened in the kara-khitans ledger.

wars.name: Atsiz's Khorasan campaign
wars.outcome: Atsiz occupies Merv, Nishapur and Sarakhs after Qatwan and is driven out by Sanjar in 1142.

wars.name: Tekish's war with Sultan-Shah
wars.outcome: Sultan-Shah holds Merv by 1180, takes Tus (1181) and is beaten by the Ghurids at Marw al-Rudh (1190); Tekish takes Nishapur (May 1187), Sarakhs (1193) and Merv (December 1193) after Sultan-Shah's death.

wars.name: Khwarezmid conquest of Persian Iraq (Battle of Rayy)
wars.outcome: Tekish takes Ray (January 1193), kills Tughril III at Rayy (4 March 1194) and holds Persian Iraq by 25 June 1194.

wars.name: Khwarezmid-Abbasid war over Persian Iraq
wars.outcome: The caliph's army takes Hamadan, Ray and (late 1195) Isfahan; Tekish wins at Hamadan on 15 July 1196 and the town surrenders on 18 July.

wars.name: Tekish's war with the Ghurids over Herat
wars.outcome: Tekish besieges Herat from Tus in 1198 and makes peace; after his death in July 1200 the Ghurids take all Khorasan.
wars.note: The Seljuk Empire page dates the Ghurid takeover to 1200.

wars.name: Tekish's Assassin campaign
wars.outcome: Tekish captures the fortress of Qahira/Arslan-Gushay after a 4-month siege but fails at Alamut; the Isma'ilis of Turshiz agree to pay 100,000 dinars and sign a truce.
wars.note: The page gives no location for Qahira; no zone is coded.

certainty.note: The oases of Khwarezm are approximate and the Syr Darya, Karakum and Khorasan frontiers are not fixed on any page; the Persian Iraq line of 1194-1199 changed hands three times (1194, late 1195, July 1196).

notes: Pages: Anushtegin dynasty, Atsiz, Ala ad-Din Tekish, Battle of Qatwan and Seljuk Empire (budget 5); the Ahmad Sanjar page, opened for the great-seljuk-empire dossier, is cited as a second page. Failed titles (no page): Atsiz_(Khwarazmshah) and Atsiz_(Khwarazm) (url_not_found; the article is 'Atsiz'). The Anushtegin page is thin: it gives 1077, the regnal table, Qatwan, Toghrul III's defeat and 1212; the Tekish and Atsiz pages carry the territory. One state or two: the Khwarezmid Empire row (khwarezmid-empire, 1202-1235) is the same line of shahs (Wikidata Q63134381, not Q486918); the dossiers name each other, a reviewer may merge. Cliopatria rows to correct: the row starts in 1094 though the governorship begins 1077 (the 1094 start is not explained by any page opened; the table's first full reign is 1097); 1094-1146 holds the lower Syr Darya forty years before Atsiz's 1138 conquest and lacks Mangyshlak; there is no shape for 1147-1151 (Khwarezm drawn as Great Seljuk); 1152-1201 lacks Mangyshlak and the Syr Darya and, more seriously, Nishapur (1187), Ray (1193), Persian Iraq (1194-1199, with the caliph's interlude 1195-1196) and the Ghurid loss of Khorasan (1200). NOT corrected though doubtful: Merv and the Turkmen plains in 1152-1179 (the pages show Sultan-Shah, not Il-Arslan or Tekish, holding Merv by 1180); Dihistan (Tekish captured it after pursuing Sultan-Shah, undated). Not coded: the 1199 Assassin campaign (Qahira has no location on the page) and Qara Khitai suzerainty over Khwarazm 1141-1156 (a vassal relation recorded by the kara-khitans ledger). The 30,000-dinar tribute is on the Qatwan page, not on the Atsiz page. Page disagreements: Hazarasp is dated to 1138 on the Sanjar page, undated on the Atsiz page and 1204 on the Anushtegin page (a different battle with the Ghurids); Atsiz's accession 1127 or 1128 (his page); Qara Khitai took Jand in 1152 (Atsiz page) while Cliopatria's 1152 shape does not hold it. Native names are from general knowledge, not from a page. Counterparts needing dossiers: Mahmud Sultan Shah's Khorasan (1172-1193), the Eldiguzids (Gokcha), the Assassins of Alamut, Mayachuq. Gazetteer names: Jand (Cend, lower Syr Darya, about 45.6 N 62.1 E: used as a coordinate radius), Sarakhs (about 36.5 N 61.2 E: coordinate radius), Persian Iraq (a union of Iranian provinces).
